objectives: Survey bioinorganic chemistry: heme, chlorophyll, B12, nitrogenase, zinc fingers, cisplatin.
Understand metals in medicine: Pt, Au, Gd contrast, technetium-99m, alpha therapy.
Cover frontier: water splitting, Mn₄CaO₅, CO₂ reduction, MOFs, AI-driven catalyst discovery.

slides.title: Bioinorganic: heme, chlorophyll, B12, nitrogenase, zinc fingers, cisplatin
slides.body:
**Bioinorganic chemistry** studies metals in biological systems. ~30% of all proteins are metalloproteins — metal-containing — and almost every essential biological process involves a metal cofactor. The field unifies inorganic + structural + mechanistic biology.

**Heme (Fe-porphyrin)**: 4-coordinate Fe(II) in protoporphyrin IX macrocycle; 5th axial ligand = proximal histidine (in hemoglobin/myoglobin) or sulfur (in cytochrome P450 cysteine thiolate).
- **Hemoglobin** (Perutz Nobel 1962): 4 subunits (α₂β₂); each with one heme; binds + transports O₂. Cooperative binding (Hill coefficient ~2.8) via T → R state transition; iron+geometry change on O₂ binding (Fe in plane vs out of plane) propagates allosterically.
- **Myoglobin** (Kendrew Nobel 1962): muscle O₂ storage; single subunit.
- **Cytochromes**: electron transport (cyt c, cyt b, cyt a) in respiratory chain (mitochondria) + photosynthesis (chloroplast). Fe oscillates Fe(II)/Fe(III).
- **Cytochrome P450**: oxidation of xenobiotics + drug metabolism + steroidogenesis. Compound I (Fe(IV)=O + porphyrin radical cation) catalyzes C-H hydroxylation. Industrial biocatalysts (engineered P450s).
- **Catalase**: 2 H₂O₂ → 2 H₂O + O₂; protects cells from oxidative damage.
- **Peroxidase**: H₂O₂-driven substrate oxidations.
- **Heme-containing sensors**: NO sensor sGC (soluble guanylate cyclase) in vasodilation; CO sensor CooA bacterial transcription regulator.

**Chlorophyll (Mg-porphyrin / chlorin)**: Mg(II) in porphyrin macrocycle (chlorin = reduced one pyrrole). Light-harvesting + electron transfer in chloroplasts + photosynthetic bacteria. Mg's role: structural (planar, predictable geometry, no redox); kept off the redox path so chlorophyll can act as antenna + electron-source pair. Chlorophyll a + b absorb blue + red, transmit/reflect green.

**B12 (cobalamin)**: Co(III) in corrin ring (4 pyrrole-like rings; analogous to porphyrin but less conjugated). 5th + 6th axial: dimethylbenzimidazole base + variable upper ligand (CN⁻ in cyanocobalamin/vitamin, methyl in methylcobalamin, 5'-deoxyadenosyl in adenosylcobalamin).
- **Methylcobalamin**: methyl transferase (methionine synthase, folate cycle).
- **Adenosylcobalamin**: radical rearrangement enzymes (methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, ribonucleotide reductase B12 class). Homolytic Co-C cleavage → 5'-dA radical → H-atom abstraction.
- **Hodgkin 1956 (Nobel 1964)** solved B12 structure by X-ray crystallography — the most complex non-protein molecular structure of the era. **Woodward + Eschenmoser 1971** total synthesis — one of the great syntheses (>100 steps, > 100 chemists, ~10 years). **Lenhert + Hodgkin 1961** discovered Co-C σ-bond.

**Nitrogenase**: enzyme that reduces N₂ to NH₃ at ambient T + P. Three variants: Mo-Fe (most active), V-Fe, Fe-only.
- **FeMo-cofactor**: [7Fe-9S-Mo-1C-1homocitrate] cluster — 'M-cluster'. Mo + Fe + 9 sulfides + interstitial C (Einsle 2011) + homocitrate.
- **P-cluster**: [8Fe-7S]; intermediate electron-transfer.
- **Catalytic cycle**: N₂ + 8 e⁻ + 8 H⁺ + 16 ATP → 2 NH₃ + H₂. Mechanism (Schrock + Hoffmann + Hoffman) involves alternating H + e⁻ delivery — possibly via Fe-H intermediates.
- **Industrial relevance**: nitrogenase does at room T + 1 atm what Haber-Bosch needs 400°C + 200 atm. Decades of effort to develop ambient nitrogen fixation; Schrock-Yandulov 2003 first molecular Mo system; Nishibayashi catalysts ongoing.

**Zinc fingers**: Zn(II) (d¹⁰, no redox, Lewis acid + structural) bound by ~4 Cys/His residues in protein loops. Common in DNA-binding transcription factors (TFIIIA, glucocorticoid receptor, p53). ~10% of all human proteins are Zn-binding.
- **Catalytic Zn**: carbonic anhydrase (CO₂ + H₂O ↔ HCO₃⁻ + H⁺; activates water as nucleophile); carboxypeptidase (peptide hydrolysis).
- **Structural Zn**: zinc fingers, MTF; rigid scaffold.
- **Zn-finger nucleases**: engineered DNA-cutting proteins; precursor to CRISPR for genome editing.

**Cisplatin** (Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂, cis): **Rosenberg 1965** discovered Pt electrode in E. coli growth experiments inhibited cell division. cis-[Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂] became the first metal-based anticancer drug (FDA 1978). Binds to N7 of guanine in DNA → 1,2- + 1,3-intrastrand crosslinks → distortion → apoptosis.
- **Mechanism**: aqueous Cl⁻ replaces ligand → Pt(NH₃)₂(H₂O)₂²⁺ active species → DNA binding.
- **Resistance**: glutathione + cellular thiols sequester Pt; nucleotide excision repair (NER) removes adducts.
- **Second-generation**: carboplatin (bidentate CBDCA leaving group, less nephrotoxic), oxaliplatin (DACH N,N + oxalate; colorectal cancer); satraplatin (oral Pt(IV) prodrug).
- ~50% of all chemotherapy regimens use Pt drugs. Major successful targets: testicular, ovarian, lung, head/neck, bladder cancers.

slides.title: Metals in medicine: Pt, Au, Gd, technetium-99m, radiopharmaceuticals, targeted α therapy
slides.body:
**Platinum chemotherapy** — see previous slide (cisplatin, carboplatin, oxaliplatin, satraplatin, picoplatin). Continuous research: dual-action Pt(IV) prodrugs + Pt-PARP inhibitor combos + Pt-targeted antibody-drug conjugates.

**Gold therapeutics**:
- **Auranofin** (Au(I)-thiosugar-PEt₃): oral rheumatoid arthritis drug since 1985 (decline in use vs methotrexate). Soft Au(I) binds protein thiols (cysteines) → modulates immune signaling. **Drug-repurposing**: anti-cancer (thioredoxin reductase inhibition), anti-parasitic (Leishmania), antibacterial (MRSA), anti-COVID (early trials).
- **Au nanoparticles + clusters**: phototherapy (near-IR plasmon absorption → photothermal ablation; AuNRs by Halas + El-Sayed); drug delivery; SERS imaging.

**Gadolinium MRI contrast agents**:
- Gd(III): 4f⁷, 7 unpaired electrons → very large magnetic moment (μ = 7.94 μ_B) → shortens T1 relaxation → bright contrast in T1-weighted MRI.
- Gd³⁺ free ion toxic (Ca²⁺ mimic); always given as a chelate.
- **Linear chelates** (Magnevist Gd-DTPA, Omniscan Gd-DTPA-BMA): older; greater Gd³⁺ release.
- **Macrocyclic chelates** (Dotarem Gd-DOTA, ProHance Gd-HP-DO3A, Gadovist/Gadavist Gd-BT-DO3A): more kinetically stable; FDA-preferred since 2017 warnings about brain Gd retention.
- Annual usage: ~50 million doses worldwide. Major imaging modality for cancer staging, MS lesions, stroke, vascular disease.

**Technetium-99m** (γ-emitter, 140 keV, t₁/₂ = 6.0 h): the workhorse diagnostic isotope; ~85% of nuclear medicine procedures.
- Generator: ⁹⁹Mo (66 hr) → ⁹⁹ᵐTc (β⁻ + γ) → ⁹⁹Tc; Mo elutes daily from a ⁹⁸Mo-loaded reactor; ⁹⁹ᵐTc is freshly available wherever needed.
- ⁹⁹ᵐTc-radiopharmaceuticals: HMPAO (brain SPECT), MAG3 (renal), MIBI (cardiac perfusion + parathyroid), bone scans (MDP, HDP).
- ⁹⁹Mo supply chain (mostly reactor-produced from highly-enriched uranium HEU) globally fragile; LEU + cyclotron + accelerator alternatives being developed.

**PET radiopharmaceuticals (β⁺-emitters)**:
- ¹⁸F (t₁/₂ 110 min): FDG (fluorodeoxyglucose) for metabolic imaging — most-used oncology agent worldwide. F-18-PSMA + F-18-FACBC for prostate cancer; F-18-amyloid for Alzheimer's.
- ⁶⁸Ga (t₁/₂ 68 min): DOTATATE (somatostatin receptor for neuroendocrine tumors), PSMA-11 (prostate cancer).
- ⁸⁹Zr (t₁/₂ 78.4 hr): antibody labeling (immuno-PET) for slow-distributing biologics.

**Therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals (β⁻ + α)**:
- **β⁻ emitters**: ¹³¹I (thyroid cancer, hyperthyroidism), ⁹⁰Y (microspheres for liver tumors; Zevalin antibody-drug conjugate), ¹⁷⁷Lu (PSMA + DOTATATE for prostate + neuroendocrine cancers; Pluvicto / Lutathera FDA-approved).
- **α emitters**: ²²³Ra (Xofigo for prostate bone metastases, first α therapeutic FDA 2013); ²²⁵Ac, ²¹³Bi, ²¹¹At, ²¹²Pb (in development).
- **Targeted alpha therapy (TAT)**: short range (~50 µm), very high LET; spares surrounding tissue. Particularly promising for micrometastases + circulating tumor cells. Clinical trials Ac-225-PSMA + Ac-225-DOTATATE producing remarkable responses in resistant cancers.
- Theranostic pairs: diagnostic + therapeutic of same molecular target (e.g., ⁶⁸Ga-PSMA imaging + ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA therapy; ⁶⁸Ga-DOTATATE + ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE) — personalized molecular oncology.

**Other metal-based drugs**:
- **Lithium carbonate**: mood stabilizer for bipolar disorder. Mechanism unknown (inositol monophosphatase inhibition? GSK3β inhibition?).
- **Bismuth compounds**: Pepto-Bismol (BiOCl basic bismuth salicylate), H. pylori eradication (Bi + antibiotics).
- **Iron chelation**: deferoxamine + deferasirox for transfusion-dependent thalassemia + sickle cell.
- **Antimony**: pentavalent Sb for leishmaniasis.
- **Arsenic trioxide**: As₂O₃ for APL (acute promyelocytic leukemia) — combined with all-trans retinoic acid gives ~90% complete remission.
- **Silver**: Ag-coated wound dressings; silver sulfadiazine for burns.
- **Vanadium**: bis(maltolato)oxovanadium(IV) BMOV — clinical trials for diabetes (insulin-mimetic).
- **Ruthenium**: NAMI-A + KP1019 (anticancer, in trials).
- **Iron-platinum + iron-iron**: emerging anticancer agents.

slides.title: Frontier: water splitting, Mn₄CaO₅, artificial photosynthesis, CO₂ reduction, MOFs, AI catalyst discovery
slides.body:
**Solar water splitting**: $2 H_2 O \to 2 H_2 + O_2$; ΔG = +474 kJ/mol; needs ~1.23 V (thermodynamic) + overpotential.
- **Photoelectrochemical cells** (Fujishima + Honda 1972): TiO₂ photoanode + Pt cathode; UV-driven; first PEC water splitting.
- **Modern photocatalysts**: BiVO₄, hematite α-Fe₂O₃, Cu₂O, perovskite oxynitrides (LaTaON₂, BaTaO₂N), 2D materials.
- **Tandem photoelectrochemistry**: dual absorber for visible-light splitting; efficiency record ~19% (NREL JCAP).
- **PV-electrolyzer integration**: PV + alkaline/PEM electrolyzer; >25% solar-to-hydrogen reported. Industrial Cu/Pt vs cheaper transition-metal-based catalysts.

**Photosystem II Mn₄CaO₅ cluster** (natural water-splitter):
- Buried in PSII reaction center; absorbs 4 photons in S-state cycle (Kok cycle); accumulates 4 oxidizing equivalents; splits 2 H₂O → O₂ + 4 H⁺ + 4 e⁻.
- Structure: Mn₄CaO₅ cluster (Umena + Kawakami + Shen 2011 by X-ray); 'distorted chair' geometry.
- Inspires synthetic OEC mimics: Christou Mn₃Ca + Mn₄Ca clusters; Agapie Mn₃CaO₄; Stahl + Lin Co₄O₄ cubanes.
- Cobalt + nickel water-oxidation catalysts (Nocera, Dempsey, Reisner): catalytic films for solar fuel.
- 'Artificial leaf' (Nocera 2011): integrated PV + cobalt OER catalyst + NiMoZn HER catalyst → on-board H₂ production.

**Electrochemical CO₂ reduction (CO₂RR)**: $\text{CO}_2 + 2H^+ + 2e^- \to \text{HCOOH}$ or → CO, CH₄, CH₃OH, C₂H₄, C₂H₅OH depending on catalyst.
- **Copper electrocatalysts** (Hori 1985+; Sargent + Nørskov + Surendranath modern): produce C₁-C₃ products including ethylene + ethanol; selectivity tunable by morphology + facets + alloying.
- **Gold + silver**: high CO selectivity (CO is platform feedstock for Fischer-Tropsch + acetate-synthesizing biology).
- **Bismuth + tin**: formate / formic acid selectivity (HCO₂⁻ is a hydrogen carrier).
- **Molecular catalysts**: Fe-porphyrin (Robert + Savéant), Co-quaterpyridine (Liu + Robert), Mn-bpy (Kubiak + Bourrez), Ni-cyclam.
- **Industrial deployment**: Twelve (CA), Carbon Engineering (BC), Climeworks (CH), Avantium (NL), CarbonCure (CA).

**Hydrogen storage in MOFs**:
- Pressure cryostorage: MOF-5, HKUST-1, MIL-101, MOF-74 — physisorption at 77 K + 100 bar gives 6-7 wt% H₂.
- Spillover catalysts: Pt + Pd nanoparticles on MOFs enhance H₂ uptake.
- DOE 2025 target: 6.5 wt% + 50 g/L volumetric — not yet routinely met under practical (room-T, low-P) conditions.

**Carbon capture by MOFs**:
- Amine-functionalized MOFs (MOF-74 series), CALF-20 (Svante industrial deployment), Mg-MOF-74, mmen-Mg₂dobpdc (Long-Smit). Selectively bind CO₂ over N₂.
- Direct air capture (DAC): Climeworks (Switzerland, 4000 t/yr Orca facility Iceland), Carbon Engineering, Heirloom, Global Thermostat, Verdox. Cost ~$200-1000/t CO₂; need < $100/t for scale.
- Point-source capture: CO₂ from flue gas of cement + steel + power plants; CALF-20 deployed.

**AI-accelerated catalyst + materials discovery**:
- **Open Catalyst Project** (Meta + CMU + collaborators, 2020+): ~134M DFT calculations on 2M+ candidate catalysts for HER, OER, CO₂RR. Neural network potentials (GemNet, EquiformerV2, MACE) predict adsorption energies with kcal-level accuracy at ~10⁴× speedup.
- **GNoME (DeepMind 2023)**: graph neural net + active-learning + DFT validation; predicted 2.2M new stable materials, ~700 synthesized for testing.
- **MatterGen + MatterSim (Microsoft 2024)**: generative model for new materials + property prediction.
- **CHGNet, M3GNet, MACE, NequIP**: universal ML interatomic potentials.
- **Autonomous laboratories**: A-Lab (LBNL, Ceder), self-driving labs at Toronto, MIT, NCSU; robots + ML + characterization closed-loop synthesizing predicted compounds + measuring properties.
- **Cross-cutting impact**: catalyst design for water splitting + CO₂ reduction + Haber-Bosch alternatives + battery cathodes + solid electrolytes + thermoelectrics; pharmaceutical materials.
- **Continuing challenges**: most ML predictions still need experimental validation; subtle defects + dynamics + interfacial chemistry not well-captured; data biases toward easy-to-make + well-studied systems.

**Inorganic chemistry's role in climate + energy + medicine remains central**: bonding theory, catalysts, materials, isotopes — every modern technology pulls from this discipline's accumulated 150 years of chemical understanding. The combined AI/inorganic frontier (ML catalysts, MOFs at scale, targeted-α therapy, artificial photosynthesis, single-molecule magnets) suggests the next decade will be transformative.

question.question: Trace the O₂ binding cycle of hemoglobin
question.goal: Explain how Fe(II)-heme binds + releases O₂ allosterically + cooperatively in hemoglobin.

steps.prompt: In deoxy-hemoglobin, Fe(II) is 5-coordinate (4 porphyrin N + 1 proximal His). Spin state + geometry?

acceptedAnswers: high-spin d⁶; Fe sits ~0.4 Å out of porphyrin plane

hints: Without 6th ligand, weak ligand field → high-spin.
HS Fe(II) ionic radius too large for porphyrin plane.
steps.reveal: **Deoxy-Hb**: Fe(II) d⁶ high-spin (4 unpaired electrons; weak field — porphyrin + 1 His provide moderate σ + π donation, but no 6th strong-field ligand). HS Fe(II) ionic radius (78 pm) too large for porphyrin cavity → Fe sits ~0.4 Å out of plane toward proximal His. Magnetically: μ ≈ 4.9 μ_B.

steps.prompt: O₂ binds. Fe + O₂ form a bent end-on Fe-O₂ (Pauling 1948 — actually a partly oxidized Fe(III)-O₂⁻ formulation, Weiss model). What spin state?

acceptedAnswers: low-spin d⁶ + Fe moves into porphyrin plane

hints: O₂ is moderately strong field → LS.
LS Fe(II) smaller → fits in plane.
steps.reveal: **Oxy-Hb**: Fe(II) d⁶ low-spin (or formally Fe(III)-O₂⁻ in the Weiss model — debate ongoing). LS Fe(II) ionic radius ~61 pm → fits within porphyrin plane. Fe moves ~0.4 Å into plane; bond to proximal His pulls F-helix. Diamagnetic (paired). The plane-shift transmits allosteric signal.

steps.prompt: How does this geometric change at one heme propagate to the other 3 subunits?

acceptedAnswers: T (tense) → R (relaxed) quaternary structure change; subunit interfaces shift; remaining hemes' affinity for O₂ increases

hints: Movement of His drags F-helix → α/β interface change.
steps.reveal: **T → R transition**: proximal His movement pulls the F-helix → subunit interfaces shift → other hemes' geometry favors O₂ binding → higher affinity. Resulting **cooperativity**: sigmoidal binding curve; Hill coefficient ~2.8; 4 hemes don't bind independently but as a coordinated system. Practical effect: Hb saturates ~98% at lung pO₂ (~100 mmHg) + releases ~25% at tissue pO₂ (~40 mmHg) → efficient O₂ delivery. Bohr effect (allosteric H⁺ + CO₂ binding) + 2,3-BPG further modulate.

steps.prompt: Why doesn't free Fe(II)-porphyrin in solution work as O₂ carrier?

acceptedAnswers: free heme oxidizes to Fe(III)-O-Fe(III) bridge (peroxo intermediate); protein 'distal pocket' prevents this

hints: What's the role of distal His + Val/Phe pocket?
steps.reveal: Free heme + O₂ rapidly forms peroxo bridge Fe(III)-O-O-Fe(III) → irreversible oxidation to Fe(III) hematin (met-Hb, useless). **Hemoglobin/myoglobin solve this** via the **distal pocket**: distal His + Val + Phe sterically prevent bimolecular collisions of two Fe-O₂ units. Distal His also H-bonds to bound O₂ (~1 kcal/mol stabilization) + disfavors CO binding (kinks linear FeCO into bent geometry, lowering CO affinity ~200-fold relative to free heme). The protein scaffold makes Fe-porphyrin a reversible, controlled, selective O₂ carrier — biology's ingenious engineering.

question.finalResult: $$\boxed{\text{Deoxy-Hb (HS Fe(II) out-of-plane) + O}_2 \to \text{Oxy-Hb (LS Fe(II) in-plane)} \to \text{T} \to \text{R cooperative O}_2 \text{ uptake}}$$ Hemoglobin (Perutz Nobel 1962) couples a simple inorganic electronic transition (HS ↔ LS spin-state) to a global quaternary protein reorganization to give cooperative + tunable O₂ transport. Inorganic principles (CFT + spin state + bond lengths) + protein engineering (distal pocket protection) produce one of biology's most-studied + most-elegant systems.

question.question: Why is the Mo-Fe nitrogenase enzyme so much more efficient than the Haber-Bosch process for nitrogen fixation, and what's the catalytic biotechnology relevance?
options: **Nitrogenase fixes N₂ at room T + 1 atm**; Haber-Bosch needs 400-500°C + 150-300 atm + ~1-2% of world's energy. **Mechanism advantage**: nitrogenase uses **alternating H + e⁻ delivery** (Lowe-Thorneley scheme; 8 H + 8 e⁻ + 16 ATP for 2 NH₃) via the **FeMo-cofactor [7Fe-9S-Mo-1C-1homocitrate]** (Einsle 2011 revealed the interstitial C); intermediate Fe-H species + protonation events lower the activation energy for N≡N cleavage. The cluster geometry + electron-storage redox states (S-state-like Kok cycle) + protein-protected pocket together orchestrate gentle stepwise reduction. **Industrial dream**: develop ambient catalysts mimicking this. **Schrock + Yandulov 2003**: first molecular Mo(III) catalyst with N₂ → NH₃ + bulky HIPT (terphenyl-amido) ligands; **Nishibayashi 2010+**: improved Mo + Fe systems with PNP pincer ligands giving 100s-1000s turnover. **Pickett + Tyler + Peters**: alternative Fe-based catalysts. **Challenges**: industrial deployment, energy efficiency comparable to or better than electrolytic Haber-Bosch, robust catalysts. Recent: electrocatalytic + photocatalytic N₂ fixation experiments; biological + biotech engineering of free-living + symbiotic diazotrophs for crops (without fertilizer addition).
question.explanation: Nitrogenase: room-T + 1 atm N₂ fixation via Mo-Fe cluster; alternating H + e⁻ delivery; 8 H + 8 e⁻ + 16 ATP per 2 NH₃. FeMo-cofactor [7Fe-9S-Mo-1C-1homocitrate] (Einsle 2011). Inspires molecular mimics (Schrock-Yandulov 2003, Nishibayashi); industrial goal of ambient-condition Haber-Bosch alternative. Massive energy + climate stakes.

hints: What's the catalytic cluster structure + how does it work?
Why does ambient T + P make this so valuable?
slides.workedSolution: Nitrogenase Mo-Fe enzyme fixes N₂ at RT + 1 atm using FeMo-cofactor [7Fe-9S-Mo-1C-1homocitrate] (Einsle 2011) + alternating H/e⁻ delivery (Lowe-Thorneley). Schrock-Yandulov 2003 + Nishibayashi modern systems are molecular mimics aiming to replace energy-intensive Haber-Bosch.

question.question: Mn₄CaO₅ and artificial photosynthesis
question.prompt: PSII oxygen-evolving complex (OEC) is a Mn₄CaO₅ cluster that splits 2 H₂O → O₂ + 4 H⁺ + 4 e⁻ at ambient conditions, charged by 4 photons (Kok S-state cycle). Synthetic OEC mimics (Christou Mn₃Ca + Mn₄CaO₄; Agapie + Bertaccini Mn₃CaO₄; Wang + Stahl Co₄O₄ cubanes) approach but don't yet match natural turnover or stability. Nocera's 'artificial leaf' (2011) integrated PV + Co catalyst + Ni-Mo-Zn HER → on-board H₂. (a) What's special about Mn₄CaO₅ that synthetic clusters struggle to replicate? (b) Why is water oxidation (OER) thermodynamically + kinetically the hardest half-reaction in solar fuel devices? (c) How might combining MOFs, AI catalyst discovery, and bioinorganic design accelerate practical artificial photosynthesis?

question.question: A patient receives 100 mCi of ⁹⁹ᵐTc (t₁/₂ = 6.0 hr) for a bone scan. How much activity (in mCi) remains 12 hours later?
question.hint: 12 hr = 2 half-lives. Activity = 100 × (1/2)² = 100 × 0.25 = 25 mCi. ⁹⁹ᵐTc's short half-life is a feature: enough for imaging, but fast clearance reduces patient dose. Generator-eluted from ⁹⁹Mo (66 hr) freshly at hospital.

question.prompt: In ≤140 words, explain how the principles of inorganic chemistry (coordination, redox, ligand-field, spectroscopy) underlie bioinorganic chemistry (heme + nitrogenase + B12 + zinc fingers + cisplatin), medical inorganic chemistry (Pt + Gd MRI + ⁹⁹ᵐTc + targeted α therapy), and the frontier (water splitting + CO₂ reduction + MOFs + AI catalysts).
question.rubric: Mentions: bioinorganic — heme Fe(II) HS↔LS coupled to allosteric Hb cooperativity (Perutz Nobel 1962); cytochromes + P450 oxidations; chlorophyll Mg-porphyrin; B12 cobalamin (Hodgkin Nobel 1964) radical chemistry; FeMo-cofactor in nitrogenase; Zn-fingers (structural + catalytic); cisplatin (Rosenberg 1965) DNA-binding chemotherapy. Medicine — Pt drugs cisplatin/carboplatin/oxaliplatin; Gd-DOTA MRI contrast (Gd³⁺ μ ≈ 7.94 μ_B); ⁹⁹ᵐTc generator-eluted SPECT (85% of nuclear medicine); ¹⁸F + ⁶⁸Ga PET radiopharmaceuticals; ¹⁷⁷Lu + ²²⁵Ac targeted radionuclide therapy; auranofin Au(I) thiol chemistry. Frontier — water splitting (TiO₂ Fujishima-Honda 1972; Mn₄CaO₅ PSII mimics; Nocera artificial leaf); CO₂ reduction electrocatalysis (Cu for C₂+; Bi for formate); MOFs (Yaghi-Robson-Kitagawa 2025 Nobel) for H₂ storage + CO₂ capture + DAC (Climeworks); AI for catalyst discovery (Open Catalyst, GNoME, MatterGen); autonomous labs. Conclude: 150 years of inorganic chemistry from Mendeleev now powers pharmaceuticals + clean energy + climate solutions.
